content:
maria: FYI canary-3 failed during a 64x batch run — OOM hitting logits allocation after the new reuse path landed. attaching short traces and a repro command. :eyes:
kevin: ugh, saw that locally too. memory profile shows a ~20% larger peak when the logits slab is sharded across streams.
sasha: is this the change that switched to 'lazy-zero' + recycle-on-free?
maria: yes — we moved to lazy-zero to avoid memset cost and introduced a recycle list per-size-class. but on heavy prefix KV workload the recycler keeps too many live small shards and we trigger a big allocate for the final logits slab. logs show: `OOM allocating logits_slab 4.1G (requested) / 4.0G available`
jen: can you paste the exact repro command? I want to run it on an infra node.
maria: run: `./run_canary --model r-infer-7b --batch 64 --prefix kv-1000 --streaming=false` — repros on g4dn-large. attached top-down flame and cudaMalloc trace.
kevin: quick idea: recycler should prefer returning small contiguous slots to a global freelist rather than holding them per-stream. per-stream caches are preventing consolidation for big final alloc.
sasha: agreed. also kernel-selection path sometimes pins logits slab to kernel-affine stream which prevents cross-stream reuse. that makes fragmentation worse.
jen: infra-bot: reserving gpu-02 for repro (eta 10m).
infra-bot: reserved gpu-02 for @jen, expires in 2h.
tom: sketch of patch: move small-slot pools to shared freelist with a 'merge-on-threshold' heuristic, and force eviction of per-stream caches when a large slab allocation fails. prototype diff: ```diff
- per_stream_pool[size].push(slot)
+ if (per_stream_pool[size].len > MERGE_THRESHOLD) move_to_global(per_stream_pool[size])
```
kevin: can we also change the allocate path to attempt compaction before fallback allocate? e.g., try reclaiming leaked prefix caches and run `cudaMemTrim()` equivalent before allocating big logits slab.
sasha: compaction + eviction order tweak should be low-risk if behind flag. let's gate under `POOL_GLOBAL_MERGE=true` and test.
maria: will try TOM's change + force-evict in a canary. also adding an instrumentation counter for 'global_merge_moves' and 'evicted_slots' so we can see behavior in traces.
jen: running a canary now with flag off (baseline) and then with 'POOL_GLOBAL_MERGE=true'. I'll post metrics.
deploy-bot: canary job 17345 started (canary-3) — baseline run queued on gpu-02.
kevin: note: there was a related perf regression in kernel-selector where it preferred a 2-stream kernel for logits if any stream had small idle slots. that heuristic should be inverted: prefer single-stream kernel for big final logits.
sasha: adding a guard in kernel-selector: if upcoming_alloc > BIG_THRESHOLD, prefer single-stream affinity.
maria: ran quick local with `POOL_GLOBAL_MERGE=true` and a manual eviction sweep. peak memory drops ~600MB and canary doesn't OOM in 3/3 runs. will push a small PR for the merge logic + metrics. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4573 :thumbsup:
jen: nice. please include a small test that simulates per-stream hold and then large allocation to catch regressions.
tom: also add a debug log when global_merge_moves > 0 to help on-call correlate.
maria: will add tests + logs. plan: flip flag on canary tomorrow AM; if stable, enable for canary-3 traffic then canary-10.
kevin: add a note to changelog and rollout docs about chunking heuristics — ops teams should know logit-slab sharding changed.
sasha: also file a follow-up to look at upstream allocator (cudaMallocAsync tuning) — this might reduce need for aggressive merges.
maria: thanks all. assigned follow-ups: PR 4573 (maria), test + logs (maria), canary flip (jen), kernel-selector guard (sasha). leaving this thread open until canary passes. :white_check_mark:
